text_blocks.snippet: Side effects from the Pfizer COVID-19 vaccine typically last for a few hours to a couple of days, with most people experiencing only mild and temporary symptoms. These side effects are a sign that your body is building immunity and are generally comparable to the side effects experienced with routine vaccinations.
snippet_highlighted_words: a few hours to a couple of days

list.title: Common side effects:
list.snippet: These include pain, redness, or swelling at the injection site, fatigue, headache, muscle pain, chills, fever, and nausea.

list.title: Duration:
list.snippet: Most side effects resolve within 1-2 days. In some cases, swollen lymph nodes may persist for up to 10 days.

list.title: Severe side effects:
list.snippet: Severe symptoms that last for 72 hours or more are rare. If you experience severe symptoms, contact your healthcare provider.

list.title: Building immunity:
list.snippet: The presence of side effects indicates that your immune system is responding to the vaccine and building protection against the virus.

list.title: No side effects:
list.snippet: If you don't experience any side effects, it doesn't mean the vaccine isn't working. Your body is still building immunity.
Rest: Allow your body time to recover.
Hydration: Drink plenty of fluids.
Over-the-counter pain relievers: Use medications like acetaminophen or ibuprofen, unless you have specific contraindications.
Cool compresses: Apply a cool, damp cloth to the injection site.
